recipes.name: Island Kielbasa in a Slow Cooker
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds kielbasa sausage, sliced into 1/2 inch pieces

steps.text: Place the sausage, ketchup, sugar and pineapple in the slow cooker and mix together.
Cook on low setting for 5 to 6 hours, until sausage is cooked through.

raw_recipe.headline: Island Kielbasa in a Slow Cooker
raw_recipe.description: Kielbasa sausage, ketchup, brown sugar and pineapple - the flavors of the islands mixed together, and left to cook up a tropical tasting dish in a slow cooker!
raw_recipe.name: Island Kielbasa in a Slow Cooker
recipeIngredient: 2 pounds kielbasa sausage, sliced into 1/2 inch pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Place the sausage, ketchup, sugar and pineapple in the slow cooker and mix together.
Cook on low setting for 5 to 6 hours, until sausage is cooked through.

review.reviewBody: I added sliced carrots, onions and peppers to the recipe and cut the brown sugar in half. The sauce was great served over rice. I did thicken it a bit with corn starch and added a little vinegar for a nice sweet/sour taste. Next time I will try it with chicken instead of the kielbasa. Great recipe.

I love this recipe for the summer! However, like many have posted, the sauce was waaay too sweet for us. I also thought it was too ketchup-y. Instead, I used 1 cup of bbq sauce, 1/2 cup of ketchup, and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. I also use fresh pineapple and add onions and green peppers. Finally, I just cook it on the stove top instead of a slow cooker. I sauté the onions and peppers until tender, add the kielbasa and the sauce and let everything simmer for about 10 minutes, then add the pineapple. It’s done when the pineapple has warmed through. We think it’s perfect!

served it over noodles. 2 1/2 # of Polish sausage, 1 cup cubed sweet onion, 1 cup cubed green pepper, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 1 (20 oz.) can chunked pineapple and 3/4 cup ketchup.
cooked the polish sausage, onion and pepper together in a Dutch oven with a tbsn of vegetable oil until onions translucent and pepper was soft. added brown sugar and ketchup and mixed. Cooked noodles, drained and mixed. Added pineapple and half the remaining pineapple juice and served. Excellent dinner for three with enough left over for another meal.

I made this for my godsons family while I was spending time with his this week. I made a few changes lol. 

First I reduced the sugar to probably 3/4 if a cup. I left the catsup at 2 cups and the pineapple was in natural juice. I only used 1 lb of need kielbasa’s. As I was running omg in her fridge I found a yellow pepper who was just begging to be used. I cut it into large strips as I didn’t want it to get too soggy. I mixed the ingredients in a lined crockpot and cooked the sauce for about 2 hours or until I could smell the pepper. I generally cook nu smell, something my mother did and I’ve taught my son also. Once I could smell the pepper I cut up the kielbasa and added it to the sauce. She let it cook for about 2 1/2 hours. I got a text message saying “wow and holy cow! I did t expect to like this, honestly, but there are no leftovers!” Enough said! I’m making it tonight for hubby and me sans pepper as I can’t eat them. I will be using swerve (sugar free) brown sugar as he is a diabetic. The pineapple again is in a NSA juice. 2 cups of brown sugar, IMHO, would overwhelm the dish and make it too sweet.

I made some changes and it turned out delicious! everybody loved it at the Thanksgiving potluck we had. I totally agree that you need to cut down on the sugar so I used about 3/4 cup with about two and a half packages of the kielbasa sausage, but you can make more or less. I browned the sausages for a few minutes in a Skillet with oil then added to the crock pot then added the brown sugar and about 1/2 cup of barbecue sauce and 1/3 c ketchup..cooked on high for about an hour then added some sweet mini yellow and red peppers cut into strips then cooked for another 2 hours on low adding the pineapples with juice about the last 30 - 45 minutes. Yum, yum! Will definitely make it like this more often.

Family loved it. Halved the recipe for 3 people. Half again for the brown sugar, pineapple chunks and pineapple juice. Slow cooked the kielbasa, ketchup , and diced red bell peppers (my addition) on high for 2 hours 
Then added the chunks, juice, and 2 Tbsp. white vinegar (for a little extra zip) for the last hour. Put on a bed of Jasmine rice. Perfecto!

This has been a go to potluck recipe of mine for at least 10 years! I’ve found that Eckrich skinless kielbasa works best. I use 1pkg kielbasa (cut into bite size pieces), 1 cup ketchup, 1 cup light brown sugar and 1 cup pineapple juice. If you look in your local juice isle, pineapple juice comes in little 6pk cans. You just use 1 can in the pack. I cooked on low for 2 hours in a crockpot, not 5. I personally don't like veggies or pineapple chunks with mine, but you can still add it in if you want. I’ve put this kielbasa and sauce over white rice, mashed potatoes, egg noodles, or just by itself as a snack. The last time I made this it was for 11 people, including me. I used 3 packages kielbasa, 3 cups ketchup, 3 cups light brown sugar and 3 cups pineapple juice. There were no leftovers, much to my husband’s dismay.

Made this and it is a great recipe. I didn't use the crockpot. I made it stove top and browned the sausage first and used 1/2 the brown sugar. It was a little soupy but the taste was great. I think I will try to add onion and green peppers next time. We served it with brown rice.

SOOOO GOOD! I went a little easy on the brown sugar using only one cup as pretty much everyone in the reviews suggested and let it cook on low for four hours but otherwise, I made this as is. If you like kielbasa and pineapple, this dish is a must-have in your life. Thank you for sharing! *******EDIT, WEEKS LATER: At least one person suggested that this same dish could be made on the stovetop. That is what I did this evening: I browned the kielbasa, added the rest of the ingredients and let 'er simmer on the stove for about an hour. Nope. It's not the same. It's barely edible, really. So you gotta go with the slow cooker on this one, folks.

I didn’t know if this called for smoked kielbasa or fresh kielbasa. I only had fresh and I didn’t want to use that so I used Butterball smoked turkey sausage. I sort of followed the recipe but made changes like others. I only use about a cup and a third of ketchup and a half cup of brown sugar. I am so glad I didn’t use more brown sugar it would’ve been way too sweet. I also added large chunks of onion and green pepper, garlic, and a little bit of Cayenne for a touch of heat. I also did not add the whole can of pineapple. I thickened it a tiny bit with corn starch. Served it over rice and it was very good although I tend not to love sweet dinners. My son chowed it with two helpings. I can see doing this with chicken or shrimp.

Per previous reviews I also cut brown sugar down to 3/4 c and ketchup to 1 1/2 c. I added bell pepper, onions and broccoli and served over rice. Instead of using the slow cooker I just cooked it on top of the stove and it was ready within an hour. Thickened with a little cornstarch. It was very good.
Delicious! Serve over noodles!
This is so simple and tasty. I serve it over rice. And I cut the brown sugar back to 1 1/4 cups. I just find 2 cups is too much.

This was pretty good but the second time I made it I used only a cup of brown sugar not two cups. I also used pineapple chunks (20oz can) in 100% juice not the heavy syrup. If you put two cups of brown sugar it makes this recipe really, really sweet and it takes away from the flavor of the pineapple and the kielbasa. I served mine over white rice because the sauce ends up really thin. I have also served these on toothpicks and I put the sauce on the side for dipping.
This recipe is easy to make, but way too sweet!

way too much sugar for me to enjoy. the fam also made similar comments without being asked. they said they will enjoy this more with less sweetness. I could barely taste the flavor of the kielbasa there was so much sugar. after making this recipe as written, I'll definitely check the sugar in half. I chose to cook this at 4 hours on low and it was just starting to get too soft. I think 3.5 hours will be the best cooking time. looking forward to trying this recipe again with better results as the foundation if ingredients is definitely great!

My husband loves this. It’s very easy and delicious. I do fix it in the crock pot, and have never had the sausage overcooked or soggy. I cut it in thick slices, and put it in after sauce has cooked on high for an an hour or so on high. We put red and or yellow bell peppers, mushrooms and sliced onions in the sauce. When we put the kielbasa in, we cook it a couple more hours on high. We always get that nice, juicy pop, when we bite into the kielbasa. I add a little hot sauce to mine, and husband enjoys it as is. Usually serve it over shell pasta or rice. As with any recipe, adjust to your own liking, but definitely give this one a try.

Something different. We were sick of all the usual dinner menus during quarantine. This was something easy and unusual. We served it over rice. We had the leftovers as toothpick appetizers another night.

I made it with a combination of chicken and kielbasa (I had 1lb). It was OK, but none of us finished off the sausage, although the kids liked and ate all the chicken. I'd prefer something a little healthier.
I cooked shell pasta and added it in for the last 10 minutes. Was great. Even my 4 year old son loved it.
